description.p: Whatevr is a native Linux WhatsApp client backed by the whatevrd background daemon.

Forwarded-message header borrowed from Telegram Desktop (bubbles show a Forwarded header; doc/tdesktop-notes.md adds the full whatkevr-vs-tdesktop verdict table). Inbound stickers now enter Recents, and the sticker picker stays open for multi-send like WhatsApp mobile (plain click sends and keeps it open, Ctrl+click closes).

p.em:
Whatevr 0.8.7

Desktop parity and workspace improvements.

## Highlights

- Persistent two-column workspace for chats, status, calls, channels, logs, and starred messages.
- Mobile-style status autoplay with embedded video playback, timed stills, and next-person progression.
- Desktop microphone voice recording through Qt Multimedia and the existing voice send path.
- Durable one-shot scheduled text messages.
- Local chat favorites and daemon-owned custom chat folders.
- Channel message loading, viewed receipts, and reactions.
- Message Info sent, delivered, read, and played details.
- Notification mark-read and capability-gated inline reply actions.
- Expanded tray menu and right-click actions.
- Frontend app lock and backup controls.

GIF provider search, multi-account support, live SQLCipher encryption, and full desktop call media remain deferred.

ul.li: Chat export: "Export chat…" in the conversation menu writes the transcript (.txt, official export shape with timestamps, names, markup, media markers) through a save dialog.
Document sends keep their real filenames end to end (regression-tested).
Tray menu is a real popup window at the click point; the icon never pulses.
Channel pages load older messages on scroll.
Status viewer refreshes the moment downloads land.
scripts/verify_features.py: local checks for every README feature row.

description.p: Screenshot-driven fixes plus the tray/status/notification follow-through.

ul.li: Logs tab actually fills now (rows carry ids), with copy actions and an open-log-folder button.
Chat media gallery filters work again, and Channels refreshes on open.
Status rings on chat avatars with tap-to-view, thumbnail avatars in the status list, and auto-download when a status opens.
Tray right-click menu fixed, unread tooltip corrected, channel posts notify, misfiled newsletter chats purged and blocked from returning.

Plus the extra-features batch: anti-delete, edit history, status keep and archive, sender client indicator, unread filter, pop-out windows, typing toggle, multi-file attach, markup shortcuts, @admins, and a new doc/ folder with build, safety, and troubleshooting guides.

description.p: Statuses, tray follow-ups, and everyday sending improvements on top of 0.8.1.

ul.li: The status@broadcast chat is back: statuses are filed there as ordinary messages alongside the Status tab, silently — no unread bump, no notification. Disable it in Settings, Chats, Status.
Old statuses gain their thumbnails automatically on connect, and video statuses now play in the viewer.
Drop files onto a conversation to send them.
Saving a profile picture prefills the chat or contact name.
The Logs page reports load failures instead of staying blank.

description.p: Fix release on top of 0.8.0: the Logs tab, status thumbnails, and the tray icon all work now.

ul.li: The Logs tab was always empty because only the command existed, not the view. The daemon.logs view now streams recent log lines into the page.
Statuses render thumbnail-first: sender thumbnails are cached at ingest, and opening a status auto-downloads the full media.
Tray left-click raises the window; right-click shows a menu with Open, a Notifications toggle, and Quit. The icon pulses only while unread chats exist.
Status rows show sender avatars instead of initials-only, and the profile-picture viewer gained a Save button.
Fixed a non-idempotent database migration, a missing import, and the chat-bubble performance test's properties and budgets.
whatsmeow pinned to the 2026-09-15 commit; no API changes.

Fixed a launch-blocking bug: since the last release the frontend failed to open at all — one QML file used a qualified QQC2.Button without its import, which made the whole interface fail to load. Whatevr now starts.
The expression picker no longer freezes on the stickers tab when switching back to emoji or closing the picker.
Sending: video, audio, voice notes and documents (not just images), view-once sending, quoted replies and caption edits for all media, and attaching any file type.
New Status tab: post text/photo/video/audio statuses, view contacts statuses with a stepped viewer, download and save them.
Calls tab: incoming 1:1 and group calls ring with a desktop notification (answer on your phone), call rejection, and missed-call tombstones.
Groups and communities: create, leave, rename, topic, photo, invite links, join by link, member management, announce/lock settings, and community sub-groups with admin link/unlink.
Backups: AES-256-GCM encrypted export bundles, offline whatevrd --restore import, and backup passphrase storage in the OS keyring (Secret Service).
Media saving: copy any chat media, status, or profile photo to a path of your choice; inbound view-once media can be saved on demand.
Polls, channels, contacts, locations and a daemon log viewer in the frontend.
Tray icon with connection state and unread indicator, rotated debug log file, and a daemon.logs query over the in-memory ring.

p.em: gRPC is dead. Long live the daemon!

description.p: After almost 2 months of work, Whatevr finally has the architecture I wanted from the start.
New stuff:

ul.li: whatkevr now talks to whatevrd over a stable, documented local protocol. One daemon, one socket, and as many frontends as you want.
Two tiny example frontends now ship with the project, including a working WhatsApp client in about 30 lines of shell.
Phone-side chat deletions and read state now sync properly, and Whatevr can ask the phone for older history.
You can edit your profile about, block contacts, open downloaded photos in the viewer, and see useful tombstones for unsupported media.
Added a setting to snap back to the newest message after sending.

description.p: Fixed stuff:

ul.li: Chats open much faster, the chat list loads lazily, and navigation and column slides are considerably smoother.
Unread counts can actually be cleared now, unread dividers land where they should, and new-message badges no longer count your own sends.
Starred messages, search results, reply quotes, and other message jumps now go to the correct message instead of vaguely opening the chat.
Fixed animated stickers turning into blocky garbage after the first frame.
Fixed custom wallpapers appearing squashed or missing while opening a chat.
Fixed encrypted message edits, changed contact identities, stalled history syncs, and several "waiting for this message" cases.
Lots of protocol hardening, ordering fixes, UI polish and regression tests.
